items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: He was with Lunceford when he got popular in New York at the Cotton Club, Thommy was, and nice looking boy. He was a fantastic trumpet player.

ctx.x: Now, in this band there was a trumpet player, high note trumpet player. He was very flashy, and his name was Stevenson. But he went with Lunceford later on. He was the first high note trumpet player that Lunceford had before Paul Webster was Stevenson. He went with -- Tommy was a fantastic trumpet player. Played a lot of high
notes. And he was with Lunceford when he got popular in New York at the Cotton Club, Thommy was, and nice looking boy. He was a fantastic trumpet player.

And we used to play a lot of battle of the bands and music with this band. They'd come to Washington. We'd go to Baltimore. And they had some good -- they had a couple of brothers, Chauncey Horton who later played with Cab Calloway. He was on that band. And Shorty Horton, his brother played -- one played the saxophone and one played trombone. And they were very good players on that band.
